A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUIT research work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, including the heatmap examples. Added material can be distinguished reliably from relocated or renumbered content.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and the appendices report original knowledge-editing experiments, capability evaluations, ablations, and subspace analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds preservation tests, RippleEdits results, larger-model evaluation, and further subspace and computation-cost analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the SVD-based key projection, two-direction residual update, directional penalty, and AlphaEdit-based weight update. Additional tuning explanations and precomputation details do not establish a changed editing algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix F.7 adds RippleEdits POPULAR, testing propagation to logically and compositionally implied facts, subject aliases, and preservation after individual edits. This substantially extends task coverage beyond direct factual editing, contextual robustness, and general-capability benchmarks retained from v1.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Table 1 and the extended CounterFact comparisons remain unchanged. Added larger-model and RippleEdits experiments reuse MEMIT and AlphaEdit, already evaluated against SUIT; no comparator is removed from a retained comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix E.2 revises the stated zsRE reference from the pre-edit model to immediately before each batch, without establishing that experiments were rerun. New protocols include preservation of the original answer's first 1–4 tokens after all edits, LLaMA2-13B with 500 edits, 100 individual RippleEdits edits, additional models for spectral analysis, and controlled subject-count and entity/context experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds zsRE metric diagnostics and stricter preservation tests, RippleEdits robustness evaluation, spectral comparisons across models, sensitivity to the number of subjects used for SVD, and controlled entity-versus-context interventions. These substantially expand validation beyond the retained component ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, perturbation measurements, and heatmaps.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new sample averages, layer averages, and distance contrasts extend the analyses without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises the Qwen zsRE results: SUIT's S changes from 88.2 to 89.3 and specificity from 96.6 to 81.7; AlphaEdit's S changes from 89.6 to 73.9, reversing their S ranking. These revisions do not establish gains under identical settings. New tables report stricter preservation, larger-model, RippleEdits, cost, and subspace results; Table 5 also adds S scores.

T1.justification: Appendix J introduces mathematical definitions for within-entity and between-entity distances, norm-normalized distances, and entity-effect contrasts. These are limited formal additions for the new analysis; the editing mathematics, assumptions, and derivations in Appendices A–C remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: constraining key and residual vectors to edit-relevant subspaces improves knowledge preservation while maintaining edit efficacy and general capabilities. Additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses the weakness of gold-referenced zsRE scores and the leniency of references reset before each batch. Appendix J qualifies the subspace interpretation: both subspaces respond to entity identity, but the entity-specific space responds more strongly. New discussions also address threshold transfer, sampling-cost tradeoffs, larger-model applicability, and ripple effects.

D1.justification: Appendix I supplies a previously absent account of precomputation resources: NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe hardware, separate key-vector and SVD timings, peak memory across subject counts, and reuse of cached factors per model and layer. v2 also documents threshold selection and controlled-analysis procedures. These are documentation additions; code and data release remains promised upon publication.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for RippleEdits, LLaMA 2, and the Kneedle algorithm, and explicitly critiques prior zsRE specificity evaluation. The main related-work section and SUIT's positioning within knowledge-editing and linear-representation research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include localized rewrites of Section 6.3, expanded dataset and metric explanations, standardized model names, and a corrected weight-decay parameter label. New appendix subsections organize the additions, while the main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds dedicated zsRE, larger-model, RippleEdits, and cost/subspace tables, plus a twenty-panel spectral figure. Table 1 shades the S columns and Table 5 gains an S column. Existing plots and the five heatmap examples are retained, with some relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central preservation and subspace claims. Compared with v1's first-token zsRE reporting and variance comparisons, it provides stricter preservation tests and controlled entity/context interventions, alongside practical cost measurements and broader evaluation. These gains outweigh a localized reporting defect: Section 5.2 still claims the highest Qwen specificity at 96.6%, although the revised Table 1 reports SUIT at 81.7% and FT-L at 89.7%.
